title: Fiber KL divergence unchanged by conditioning on the special Y-bit
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the disjointness function on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$, recording the transcript, the special coordinate $T$, Alice's bits before $T$, and Bob's bits after $T$. Write $\mu_z$ for the hard distribution conditioned on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$, and let $U$ be the uniform law on one bit. Suppose the event that Bob's bit $Y_T$ at the special coordinate equals $\mathrm{false}$ has nonzero probability under $\mu_z$. Then the Kullback–Leibler divergence from $U$ of the law of Alice's special bit $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ equals the Kullback–Leibler divergence from $U$ of the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ additionally conditioned on the event $\{Y_T = \mathrm{false}\}$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length n
z is an achievable value of the variable Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})
under the fiber measure, the event {Y_T = false} has nonzero probability
replaced: After rectangle switching, Alice's \texttt{xFiberKL} can be computed by first conditioning on $Y_{T}=false$ inside the $Z=z$ fiber.
